title: Demolish scenario omits sel_pipe — silently presets pipe 0 selected instead of no selection
evidence:
// 8. demolish — mouse+keys: draw, click-select the pipe, X demolishes it
	append(&sc, Parity_Scenario{
		name = "input_parity_demolish",
		tier = tier_std,
		mouse = frames(
			evs(inp.Mouse_Press{pos = n0, button = .Left}),
			evs(inp.Mouse_Release{pos = n1, button = .Left}),
			evs(inp.Mouse_Press{pos = mid01, button = .Left}),
			evs(inp.Mouse_Release{pos = mid01, button = .Left}),
			evs(inp.Key_Press{key = .X}),
		),
detail: Every sibling scenario sets `sel_pipe = -1, // no preset selection` (or 0 deliberately in class_cycle); demolish alone omits it. Odin zero-initializes i64 to 0, so drive_parity runs with pipe 0 pre-selected — the click-select step is not exercised from a clean state and X would demolish regardless.
recommended_fix: Add `sel_pipe = -1, // no preset selection` to the input_parity_demolish literal, matching the other 15 no-preset scenarios.

title: sel_pipe field comment claims "0 = none selected" but all usage treats -1 as none and 0 as a real preset
evidence:
sel_pipe: i64, // preset selection (0 = none selected)
---
		sel_pipe = -1, // no preset selection
---
		sel_pipe = 0, // a preset selection (the class keys gate on it)
---
		if r, ok := find(runs, devs, .Touch); ok && (r.drag_active || r.sel_pipe != -1 || r.sel_node != -1) {
detail: The struct doc says 0 means none, yet 16 scenarios write -1 for "no preset selection", class_cycle writes 0 as "a preset selection", and the pan/reject asserts treat -1 as the unset value. The stale comment directly misleads a reader about the demolish omission.
recommended_fix: Correct the field comment to `// preset selection (-1 = none selected)` to match init, drive_parity, and every scenario/assert.

title: Reject scenario asserts selection-unchanged with && — a change to only one of sel_node/sel_pipe passes silently
detail: The failure message says "must not change the selection", but the && condition only fires when BOTH selectors changed; a node-only or pipe-only change is accepted. The pan case one hunk earlier enforces the same no-op semantics with ||.
recommended_fix: Change the reject guard to `r.sel_node != -1 || r.sel_pipe != -1` so either selection mutation fails, matching the message and the pan case.

title: Parity_Run.last_reject is captured for "the rejection scenario" but never read; the .Terminal_To_Terminal claim is never asserted
detail: drive_parity populates last_reject and the struct comment assigns it to the rejection scenario, yet no check reads r.last_reject anywhere in the file. The scenario's headline pin — the draw validates as .Terminal_To_Terminal — is asserted nowhere; only no-command and selection are checked.
recommended_fix: Assert `r.last_reject == .Terminal_To_Terminal` in the input_parity_reject case, or delete the dead field and its population.

title: check_states header comment documents class_cycle as "mouse == 0" but the case body and scenario demand 1 for both
detail: The summary comment says mouse ends at class 0; the case body fails unless mouse sel_class == 1, and the scenario comment says both "reach the same shared class state". One hunk was updated, the doc comment was missed.
recommended_fix: Update the doc comment to `class_cycle (both == 1 — the 2 key SETS 1, L_Bumper CYCLES 0 -> 1)`.

title: memlog claims "harness input-parity (11 scenarios)" while the same diff defines 17 numbered scenarios
detail: build_scenarios appends seventeen explicitly numbered scenarios (// 1. draw through // 17. pad_cursor). The new memlog entry, added in this same diff, records eleven — stale count from before the review-fix scenarios landed.
recommended_fix: Update the memlog entry to `harness input-parity (17 scenarios)`.

title: Stories file says "PR open"; memlog says "Next: commit + PR" — contradictory states in one commit
evidence:
+- **Status:** implemented 2026-08-16 — PR open (the `app/input` intent layer: raw device
---
+- JOB 5.4 done-design: ... All gates green. Next: commit + PR.
detail: Both prose files are dated 2026-08-16 and added in the same diff; one records the PR as already open, the other lists commit+PR as future work. The two status records cannot both be current.
recommended_fix: Reconcile: either amend the memlog tail to record the PR as opened, or drop "PR open" from the story status until true.

title: parity.odin imports core:os but never references it
evidence:
import "core:fmt"
import "core:os"
import rl "vendor:raylib"
import pp "../core"
import rnd "../app/render"
import inp "../app/input"
detail: No `os.` symbol appears anywhere in the 858 added lines of parity.odin — output uses fmt.printf/tprintf and os.exit lives in main.odin. Dead import in the new file.

title: Scenario frame dynamic arrays (sc.mouse/touch/pad) are never freed — only their inner slices are
detail: frames() heap-allocates the outer [dynamic][]inp.Device_Event per device, but the cleanup deletes only the inner frame slices and sc.expected. The three outer dynamic arrays per scenario leak (harmless at process exit, but the file otherwise documents careful ownership).

title: check_lane_emphasis comment claims "the equality check already proved it" but it runs before check_scenario
detail: The comment asserts the cross-device log equality was already established when check_lane_emphasis runs, yet the call site invokes it strictly before check_scenario. The stated proof ordering is false (moot today since lane is mouse-only).
recommended_fix: Either move the lane block after the check_scenario gate, or reword the comment to not claim a proof that has not happened yet.
